why: Text (Wahapedia Ultramarines, Army Rules, word for word in data.js): selected “At the start of your Command phase”; the doctrines are an advance move that does not prevent a charge (Movement, Charge), [ASSAULT] on ranged attacks (Shooting), a fall-back move that does not prevent shooting or a charge (Movement, Shooting, Charge). Command + Movement + Shooting + Charge is every phase the words name; no Fight-phase effect. The other approved choice rule, Martial Ka’tah, also stores at:'Start of your Command phase'; this one has no at (not part of this judgement, see the report).

Text (Wahapedia Ultramarines, Army Rules, word for word in data.js): selected “At the start of your Command phase”; the doctrines are an advance move that does not prevent a charge (Movement, Charge), [ASSAULT] on ranged attacks (Shooting), a fall-back move that does not prevent shooting or a charge (Movement, Shooting, Charge). All of it is your turn: advance and fall-back moves are made in your Movement phase (09.02), declaring a charge is your Charge phase, and [ASSAULT] only matters for shooting after an advance. Nothing is used in the opponent’s turn, so 'your' (no turns map needed).

“At the start of the battle round, if a model with this ability is your WARLORD, gain 1CP.” Filed under Command with at:'Start of the battle round', the settled convention (Doctrina Imperatives, Harbingers of Dread, derive.js start-battle-round).

“At the start of the battle round, if a model with this ability is your WARLORD, gain 1CP.” The start of the battle round comes before either player’s turn (07.01): 'either', as for Doctrina Imperatives.

why: Shock and Assault Disembark Moves (18.07, 18.06) are move types; Core Rules 18.03: a unit disembarks “In the active player’s Movement phase” by making a disembark move, and 09.02 lists move types as what a unit selected to move does. Shock disembark’s AFTER MOVING: “not eligible to declare a charge until the end of the turn”. Movement + Charge (the charge restriction) is what the words name. The text in data.js is Wahapedia’s word for word, including its order (Shock before Assault).

Or: If the assault doctrine is active for your unit, [Lance] and +1 AP.” kind melee, when “Fight phase, selected to fight”, note “[LANCE] (or, if the assault doctrine is active for your unit, [LANCE] and +1 AP)”: both branches and their condition are kept, nothing added. I ran index.html’s dmEffects on the note: it returns null (the condition words are left over), so the Damage tab lists it as not counted and never adds +1 AP without the doctrine. That is honest; a pick ([LANCE] / [LANCE] and +1 AP, the player says which) would let it count, an option for later, not an error.

EFFECT: a destroyed model, if the unit has not been selected to fight this phase, D6 with +1 if the assault doctrine is active; on a 4+ it is not removed until the unit has fought or the end of the phase, whichever comes first. The def “Fight phase, before it has been selected to fight: a destroyed model stays on a D6 of 4+ (+1 with the assault doctrine active) until it has fought or the end of the phase” keeps the condition, the roll, the modifier and both end points (“until X or Y” = the first of them). Same shape as the approved Hatred Eternal / Total Carnage defs.

Gist keeps WHEN (Fight phase, an enemy unit targets your ADEPTUS ASTARTES unit), the condition (not yet selected to fight), the D6 with +1 for the assault doctrine, and the 4+ result with both removal points. “removed only when your unit has fought or at the end of the phase” = the text’s “whichever comes first”. Nothing added.

“Friendly KILL TEAM units with this ability”: needs {all:['Kill Team']}. The Deathwatch Terminator Squad has the Kill Team keyword (DATASHEETS kw).

Furor: kind all, “Furor Tactics (the devastator doctrine is active for your unit)”, [SUSTAINED HITS 1]; Malleus: kind all, “(the tactical doctrine is active for your unit)”, [LETHAL HITS]. Both quote the condition and give it to the player’s tick, nothing added. Two boxes, not one pick, is right here: only one doctrine is normally active (“Unless otherwise stated”), but this list has rules that make a second one active (Author of the Codex, Codex Adept), so both can hold at once. Purgatus is left out. The calculator can allocate [PRECISION] to a picked CHARACTER (calc.js ctx.precision), but index.html never passes that, so for the app it really changes no numbers. That matches the approved Ka’tah convention of leaving out what changes no numbers. I checked dmEffects: “[SUSTAINED HITS 1]” → sus 1, “[LETHAL HITS]” → lethal.
